title: POC: deployment-mode tradeoffs (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) - Kapstone Logistics
summary: Initial POC scoping to choose deployment mode for Kapstone's document-parsing and routing ML service. Discussed success criteria (latency, throughput, privacy), workload sizing, bench plan, timelines and security requirements. AE+SE presented tradeoffs between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private; customer asked for benchmarks on 99th percentile latencies and token-cost estimates. Agreed on next steps: Redwood to share benchmark plan, price ballpark, SOC2 + KMS notes; customer to share sample workload and traffic profile.
action_items: Ava Chen - Send benchmark plan + example scripts - due 2026-10-02
Marcus Lee - Prepare a Dedicated vs Hosted latency/cost back-of-envelope for Kapstone profile - due 2026-10-05
Priya Narang - Share 1 week traffic trace and sample documents (anonymized) - due 2026-10-04
next_steps: Redwood to share POC plan and pricing range
Kapstone to provide workload sample and SLO thresholds
Schedule 60-min technical bench kickoff with Kapstone infra (Marcus + Sanjay) week of 2026-10-05
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-30
Start time: 15:30 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Ava Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Priya Gomez (Redwood SE), Priya Narang (Kapstone Head of ML), Daniel Ortiz (CTO), Sanjay Rao (Infra Lead), Lina Park (PM)

Summary (auto): initial scoping call to choose footprint for POC: hosted vs dedicated vs private; cover success criteria, bench metrics, timeline, security checklist

00:00 - Ava Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, quick roll call and then we'll jump into the POC goals. we got about 50 minutes, ok?
00:10 - Daniel Ortiz: yep good here, thanks
00:12 - Priya Narang: hi all, excited to dig in
00:18 - Ava Chen: awesome. quick context: Kapstone wants to run a document parser + routing model for incoming invoices & shipment docs. goal is reduce manual triage and improve SLA on routing. primary decision: hosted (Redwood API) vs Dedicated reserved GPUs vs Private VPC/on-prem. Marcus will run through tradeoffs and bench plan.
00:35 - Marcus Lee: thanks ava. hi all. i'll outline the high-level constraints we usually see - latency targets, throughput, data residency and cost. then propose a short benchmark hack to help pick the mode. sound good?
00:45 - Sanjay Rao: perfect. our non-negotiables: data cannot persist in third-party storage unencrypted, and we need audit logs for requests. also peak bursts around end of month - can triple qps.
01:05 - Marcus Lee: noted. so success criteria from what i heard: 95th/99th latency under X ms (we should capture a number), throughput for steady-state and burst, and security controls (KMS integration, SOC2 logs). can you confirm thresholds?
01:25 - Priya Narang: for latency we want P99 under 1.2s for the parse endpoint. steady throughput ~60 rps with bursts to ~180 rps for 5-10 minutes. cost target is more fuzzy but want to avoid 3x current infra spend.
01:45 - Ava Chen: great, that's helpful. quick clarifying q: is the 1.2s P99 measured from receipt of file to parsed JSON, including OCR? or post-OCR?
02:05 - Priya Narang: includes OCR and parsing. OCR is part of the pipeline - we may send text to Redwood or pre-process in-house. still TBD.
02:18 - Marcus Lee: that matters for model size. if you're doing OCR in-house and sending text, token counts drop a lot. if you send full documents we treat that differently - longer context.
02:30 - Lina Park: we prefer to keep OCR in-house due to accuracy reasons. so we'll send text chunks.
02:40 - Daniel Ortiz: also we need to support redaction and pii handling - detokenization hints, i don't know the term - basically we need guaranteed zero retention for pii.
02:52 - Marcus Lee: understood. Redwood Platform supports no-persist mode for hosted APIs but with some caveats for caching. dedicated and private give more control; private with customer-managed KMS gives strongest guarantees. there may be tradeoffs on autoscaling and cost.
03:20 - Ava Chen: ok let's put the three modes on the table quickly:
    - Hosted API: fastest to market, pay-as-you-go, Redwood handles scaling, includes SOC2, but persistence & KMS options limited vs private. can do no-store but prefix caching might remain for perf unless disabled (affects latency/cost).
    - Dedicated: reserved GPU capacity in our infra for your account. predictable throughput, can be configured with stricter isolation and retention policies, and we can provide dedicated logs; still managed by Redwood control plane but isolation reduces noisy neighbor.
    - Private (VPC / on-prem): full customer-managed deployment, can hook up to your KMS/HSM, network isolation, full audit control. more setup time and infra ops on your side.
03:58 - Sanjay Rao: what's the typical lead time for private? and for Dedicated?
04:05 - Marcus Lee: Dedicated can be stood up in 1-2 weeks once contract and capacity are confirmed. Private VPC on cloud usually 3-6 weeks for a POC (account teams + infra coordination). On-prem pack can be longer depending on procurement.
04:22 - Priya Narang: those timelines are rough—good to know. our procurement window is end of Q4, so we need to prove feasibility by mid-November.
04:35 - Ava Chen: that aligns ok - a 4 week POC kicking off first week of October lands us mid-November for results.
04:45 - Marcus Lee: proposed bench plan: 1) define sample corpus + token distribution 2) run perf bench on small representative model (open model or Redwood-verified) in hosted to collect baseline 3) run on Dedicated config tuned for batching and KV cache 4) run private variant if required. we'll measure latencies (p50/p95/p99), tail variance, throughput, token cost per 1k, and memory footprint.
05:15 - Daniel Ortiz: what models do you recommend for parsing tasks? small LLM + retrieval vs larger?
05:25 - Marcus Lee: typical is a mid-sized instruction-tuned model (6–13B), sometimes we pair with local vector DB for retrieval. For pure parsing, smaller models with good structuring capability might be fine; we'll include a couple of candidates in the bench. quantized variants for Dedicated reduce GPU memory and cost.
05:45 - Priya Narang: question on KV cache - does Redwood maintain like a long-lived key-value cache across requests? any privacy risks?
06:00 - Marcus Lee: good callout. KV cache here means transient attention cache per session to reduce repeated compute for long conversations; not persisted to storage. but we also have optional prefix caching which can store frequent prefixes. prefix cache can be disabled for privacy. apologies we sometimes call it K V cash or KV — transcription may confuse that.
06:25 - Sanjay Rao: for compliance we need KMS integration and ability to rotate keys, plus audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. do you support customer-managed keys currently?
06:35 - Marcus Lee: yes for Private we support customer-managed KMS/HSM. For Dedicated we offer bring-your-own-key with limited rotation APIs; for Hosted we have a managed KMS but can do enterprise integrations for some plans. we'll share the security note.
06:55 - Priya Narang: ok good. also SOC2 type 2 and ISO are required — do you have both?
07:05 - Ava Chen: Redwood has SOC2 Type II and is pursuing ISO currently; we'll attach our most recent attestation.
07:12 - Lina Park: how will benchmarking mimic your end-of-month burst? we need realistic ramp tests.
07:20 - Marcus Lee: bench plan includes steady-state at 60 rps and simulated bursts to 180 rps; we'll run multiple bursts to measure autoscaling and tail latencies. for Hosted we can simulate spike traffic; for Dedicated we'll test configured burst capacity and for Private we'll coordinate with your infra team.
07:38 - Daniel Ortiz: curious about cost estimates—ballpark per million tokens for Hosted vs Dedicated?
07:45 - Ava Chen: we'll send ranges; Hosted has per-token pricing and we can estimate from your token counts. Dedicated amortizes reserved capacity and looks better for sustained load; we'll include a back-of-envelope comparing your load profile.
08:00 - Priya Narang: one more: what about model rollouts and fallback? if a bigger model saturates we want automatic fallback to smaller model to keep latency SLOs.
08:12 - Marcus Lee: Redwood has rollout policies—can do canary, A/B, and automatic fallback to compatible variants. That's supported across Hosted and Dedicated; Private can include the same control plane features if connected back to Redwood control plane or via local configuration. small caveat: private fully air-gapped loses automatic fallback unless we configure a local variant set.
08:35 - Sanjay Rao: who owns the evaluation harness? do you provide scripts to replay traffic and measure p99?
08:42 - Marcus Lee: yes we'll provide benchmark harness (k6 or JMeter examples), model selection scripts, and a sample tokenization estimator. we'll share that repo link and a short runbook.
08:58 - Priya Narang: transcription glitch - you said k6? is that supported?
09:03 - Marcus Lee: yes, k6 or locust, whichever you prefer. our perf team uses k6 a lot for these benches.
09:12 - (brief crosstalk) Speaker 1: yeah ok
09:20 - Ava Chen: timeline recap: if you can share sample traffic by 10/4, we can run a hosted baseline the week of 10/5, and then run Dedicated config in parallel the week of 10/12. can we confirm that?
09:35 - Priya Narang: sounds reasonable. we can get sample logs anonymized by 10/4.
09:40 - Daniel Ortiz: procurement note: we'll need a SOW for Dedicated or Private with timeline and costs to sign off.
09:48 - Ava Chen: sure, we'll produce a POC SOW with acceptance criteria: P99 < 1.2s, sustain 60 rps steady, survive bursts to 180 rps under 1.8s tail latency. those acceptance numbers can be adjusted after initial baseline.
10:05 - Marcus Lee: technical nuance: if OCR remains in-house token counts will be maybe 200–800 tokens per doc average; if you send full text with noise might be higher. that'll affect batching strategy and kernel choices. we'll capture token distribution from your sample.
10:25 - Sanjay Rao: on Dedicated vs Private tradeoff—if we go Dedicated can we still require customer-managed keys for storage?
10:33 - Marcus Lee: for Dedicated we can offer a bring-your-own-key flow for data at rest; some realtime path keys are still managed by Redwood unless we run Private. we'll put specifics in the security note.
10:50 - Ava Chen: final quick questions?
10:52 - Lina Park: curious about monitoring: are you exposing per-route latency and token breakdown at token-level?
11:00 - Priya Gomez: yep. Redwood Console exposes per-route token usage, token cost, latency breakdowns and traces. We'll grant a short demo of console in next call.
11:12 - Daniel Ortiz: ok that's useful. also add a benchmark for memory footprint so we can plan instance sizing.
11:20 - Marcus Lee: yes we'll capture GPU memory utilization and peak model memory.
11:30 - Priya Narang: thank you. this feels like a good next step.
11:35 - Ava Chen: recap of next steps (out loud): Redwood to send bench plan + bench harness + security attestation + ballpark pricing; Kapstone to send anonymized traffic, we schedule technical kickoff for bench week of 10/5. Action items noted in chat.
11:55 - Daniel Ortiz: thanks everyone.
12:00 - Meeting end

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings: K V cache/KV cash, SAML pronounced as 'sammel' in a few spots, proper nouns like model names not finalized.

Attachments referenced: benchmark-plan.md (to be shared), redwood-security-overview.pdf (SOC2 note), sample-bench-harness repo link (short link to be emailed)
